correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the formula: the exact nonzero prime-field character correlation is -chi_p(8), zero branches r=0 and 8r+1=0 each contribute the explicitly calculated valuation count, and other classes lift uniformly. The dyadic image is all residues using valuation of (b-a)(a+b+1)/2; 2-adic unit-square counting and CRT give unrestricted composite result. The rational prime excess follows by direct substitution. No unproved lemmas or finite-experiment extrapolation are required. Replayed standalone exact Python checker passed 1999 moduli, 34 primes for excess, and 34 additional prime powers.

originality.rationale: The nearest specifically named observable, nonsquare excess, is defined and plotted empirically by Ulness (2022, §7.2), including rational fits by congruence class; the paper passages inspected do not give this exact three-branch law or the full prime-power/CRT classification. Wright (2013) treats quadratic-residue patterns in prime distributions, and Wang–Sun (2015) treats sums-of-forms representation counts; neither is a statement about this modular image intersection. Historical priority remains uncertain, especially from uninspected passages and terminology variants.

value.rationale: The exact intersection is the natural invariant needed for Ulness’s published nonsquare-excess statistic. The all-modulus formula is a complete classification distinguishing generic prime lifts, two singular p-adic branches, and dyadic saturation. It turns three empirical p-congruence-class curves into exact rational functions and allows any composite modulus to be evaluated without enumeration. No paper-sized consequence or universal bound is claimed; its scientific use is to quantitatively explain a published unexplained image statistic.
